algebra-distributive-partial.label: Distributed to the first term only
algebra-distributive-partial.watchFor: Draw the area model — the outside factor touches BOTH terms.
algebra-distributive-partial.student: The number outside the parentheses has to multiply BOTH terms inside, not just the first one. Draw the area model and check both pieces.
algebra-distributive-partial.studentEs: El número fuera del paréntesis debe multiplicar AMBOS términos de adentro, no solo el primero. Dibuja el modelo de área y revisa las dos partes.

coord-xy-swapped.label: Swapped the x and y coordinates
coord-xy-swapped.labelEs: Intercambió las coordenadas x e y
coord-xy-swapped.watchFor: Have them trace the horizontal move with a finger before the vertical one.
coord-xy-swapped.student: The two numbers traded places. In an ordered pair the first number is the across move and the second is the up-or-down move. Trace across first, then up.
coord-xy-swapped.studentEs: Los dos números cambiaron de lugar. En un par ordenado, el primer número es el movimiento horizontal y el segundo el vertical. Muévete primero de lado y luego hacia arriba o abajo.

decimal-place-value.label: Right digits, wrong magnitude
decimal-place-value.watchFor: Estimate to the nearest whole first, then count decimal places out loud.
decimal-place-value.student: Your digits are right — the decimal point landed in the wrong spot. Round to the nearest whole number first and see roughly where the answer should sit.
decimal-place-value.studentEs: Tus dígitos están bien: el punto decimal quedó en el lugar equivocado. Redondea al número entero más cercano y fíjate más o menos dónde debe caer la respuesta.

equation-answered-with-given-number.label: Answered with a number already in the equation
equation-answered-with-given-number.labelEs: Respondió con un número que ya estaba en la ecuación
equation-answered-with-given-number.watchFor: Ask them to substitute their answer back into the original equation out loud.
equation-answered-with-given-number.student: That number is already in the equation — it is the amount being added, or the number you divide by. The unknown is the one nobody told you. Put your answer back into the equation and see whether both sides match.
equation-answered-with-given-number.studentEs: Ese número ya está en la ecuación: es la cantidad que se suma o el número entre el que se divide. La incógnita es la que nadie te dio. Sustituye tu respuesta en la ecuación y fíjate si los dos lados coinciden.

equation-not-inverse-operation.label: Did not undo the operation
equation-not-inverse-operation.watchFor: Have them name the operation acting on the variable BEFORE they touch both sides.
equation-not-inverse-operation.student: To get the variable alone you have to undo what is being done to it, and that means the opposite operation. Doing the same one again — multiplying a second time, adding again — moves you further away. What is happening to the variable right now?
equation-not-inverse-operation.studentEs: Para dejar sola la variable hay que deshacer lo que se le está haciendo, y eso significa la operación opuesta. Repetir la misma —multiplicar otra vez, sumar otra vez— te aleja más. ¿Qué le está pasando a la variable ahora mismo?

exponent-as-multiplication.label: Multiplied the base by the exponent
exponent-as-multiplication.labelEs: Multiplicó la base por el exponente
exponent-as-multiplication.watchFor: Expand it once — write out every factor before evaluating.
exponent-as-multiplication.student: It looks like you multiplied the base by the exponent. 2³ means 2 × 2 × 2 — write out every factor before you evaluate.
exponent-as-multiplication.studentEs: Parece que multiplicaste la base por el exponente. 2³ significa 2 × 2 × 2: escribe todos los factores antes de calcular.

factorization-stopped-early.label: Stopped factoring before every factor was prime
factorization-stopped-early.labelEs: Dejó de factorizar antes de que todos los factores fueran primos
factorization-stopped-early.watchFor: Point at each factor and ask: can this one still be broken apart?
factorization-stopped-early.student: That is a correct factor pair, but not the PRIME factorization — at least one of your factors still breaks down. Keep splitting every branch until it ends on a prime.
factorization-stopped-early.studentEs: Ese es un par de factores correcto, pero no la descomposición en factores PRIMOS: al menos uno de tus factores todavía se puede separar. Sigue separando cada rama hasta que termine en un primo.

factors-multiples-confused.label: Confused factors with multiples
factors-multiples-confused.watchFor: Ask which number divides which — factors go INTO it, multiples come OUT of it.
factors-multiples-confused.student: Those are multiples — where you land counting BY the number. Factors are the numbers that divide INTO it evenly. 12 has factors 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12; its multiples are 12, 24, 36, 48.
factors-multiples-confused.studentEs: Esos son múltiplos: donde caes al contar DE ese número en ese número. Los factores son los números que lo dividen exactamente. El 12 tiene factores 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 y 12; sus múltiplos son 12, 24, 36, 48.

fraction-added-denominators.label: Added the denominators
fraction-added-denominators.watchFor: Return to a bar model — thirds plus fifths cannot become eighths.
fraction-added-denominators.student: It looks like you added the bottom numbers too. Thirds plus fifths cannot turn into eighths — draw the bars and check what size the pieces really are.
fraction-added-denominators.studentEs: Parece que también sumaste los números de abajo. Tercios más quintos no pueden volverse octavos: dibuja las barras y revisa de qué tamaño son las piezas.

fraction-no-reciprocal.label: Divided fractions without inverting
fraction-no-reciprocal.watchFor: Ask them to check with a whole-number case they already trust.
fraction-no-reciprocal.student: You multiplied the fractions just as they were written. When you divide by a fraction, the second one flips first.
fraction-no-reciprocal.studentEs: Multiplicaste las fracciones tal como estaban escritas. Cuando divides entre una fracción, primero se invierte la segunda.

fraction-straight-across-division.label: Divided numerators and denominators straight across
fraction-straight-across-division.watchFor: Reground division as “how many of these fit into that?”
fraction-straight-across-division.student: You divided the tops and the bottoms straight across. Dividing asks “how many of these fit into that?” — try that question on a whole-number case you already trust.
fraction-straight-across-division.studentEs: Dividiste los de arriba y los de abajo directamente. Dividir pregunta “¿cuántos de estos caben en aquello?” — prueba esa pregunta con números enteros que ya conoces.

geom-surface-area-as-volume.label: Found the volume instead of the surface area
geom-surface-area-as-volume.labelEs: Halló el volumen en vez del área total
geom-surface-area-as-volume.watchFor: Ask what the unit has to be — square units cover a surface, cubic units fill a space.
geom-surface-area-as-volume.student: That is the volume — the space inside. Surface area is the wrapping: find the area of all six faces and add them. Check your unit, too — a surface is measured in square units, not cubic.
geom-surface-area-as-volume.studentEs: Eso es el volumen: el espacio de adentro. El área total es la envoltura: halla el área de las seis caras y súmalas. Revisa también la unidad: una superficie se mide en unidades cuadradas, no cúbicas.

geom-triangle-area-no-half.label: Found base × height but forgot the half
geom-triangle-area-no-half.labelEs: Calculó base × altura pero olvidó la mitad
geom-triangle-area-no-half.watchFor: Draw the rectangle around the triangle — the triangle is half of it.
geom-triangle-area-no-half.student: You multiplied base × height, but that gives the whole rectangle. A triangle is half of that rectangle — take half of your answer.
geom-triangle-area-no-half.studentEs: Multiplicaste base × altura, pero eso da el rectángulo completo. Un triángulo es la mitad de ese rectángulo: toma la mitad de tu respuesta.

geom-volume-added-dimensions.label: Added the dimensions instead of multiplying
geom-volume-added-dimensions.labelEs: Sumó las dimensiones en vez de multiplicarlas
geom-volume-added-dimensions.watchFor: Build one layer of unit cubes first, then count the layers.
geom-volume-added-dimensions.student: You added length + width + height. Volume fills the box with cubes — build one layer, then multiply by how many layers stack up.
geom-volume-added-dimensions.studentEs: Sumaste largo + ancho + alto. El volumen llena la caja con cubos: arma una capa y multiplica por cuántas capas se apilan.

inequality-boundary-inclusion.label: Boundary value wrongly included or excluded
inequality-boundary-inclusion.labelEs: Valor límite incluido o excluido por error
inequality-boundary-inclusion.watchFor: Have them test the boundary value itself — does it make the statement true?
inequality-boundary-inclusion.student: The direction is right; what is off is whether the boundary number itself counts. Test that exact number in the inequality. If it makes a true statement it belongs in the set — a filled circle, ≤ or ≥. If not, it stays out.
inequality-boundary-inclusion.studentEs: La dirección está bien; lo que falla es si el número límite cuenta o no. Prueba ese número exacto en la desigualdad. Si la hace verdadera, pertenece al conjunto: círculo relleno, ≤ o ≥. Si no, queda fuera.

inequality-direction-flipped.label: Right boundary, symbol reversed
inequality-direction-flipped.watchFor: Ask which moves can flip a symbol — adding and subtracting never do.
inequality-direction-flipped.student: You found the right boundary number, but the symbol ended up pointing the other way. Adding or subtracting the same amount on both sides never changes which way an inequality points. Check the original symbol and keep it.
inequality-direction-flipped.studentEs: Encontraste el número límite correcto, pero el símbolo terminó apuntando al otro lado. Sumar o restar la misma cantidad en ambos lados nunca cambia hacia dónde apunta una desigualdad. Revisa el símbolo original y consérvalo.

inequality-graph-direction.label: Graph shaded toward the wrong side
inequality-graph-direction.labelEs: Gráfica sombreada hacia el lado equivocado
inequality-graph-direction.watchFor: Make them test one number from the shaded side out loud before accepting a graph.
inequality-graph-direction.student: The shading is on the wrong side of the boundary. Pick any number from the shaded part and put it into the inequality — if it makes a false statement, the shading belongs on the other side.
inequality-graph-direction.studentEs: El sombreado está del lado equivocado del límite. Escoge cualquier número de la parte sombreada y ponlo en la desigualdad: si resulta falso, el sombreado va del otro lado.

measure-area-perimeter-swap.label: Swapped area and perimeter
measure-area-perimeter-swap.watchFor: Ask what the unit should be — units or square units?
measure-area-perimeter-swap.student: Area and perimeter got swapped. Check the unit you should end with — plain units, or square units?
measure-area-perimeter-swap.studentEs: Se confundieron área y perímetro. Revisa con qué unidad debes terminar: ¿unidades o unidades cuadradas?

op-added-instead-of-multiplied.label: Added when the problem multiplies
op-added-instead-of-multiplied.watchFor: Ask what the operation *does* to the quantity before they compute.
op-added-instead-of-multiplied.student: It looks like you added those two numbers. This one is asking for groups of something, which means multiplying. How many groups are there, and how big is each one?
op-added-instead-of-multiplied.studentEs: Parece que sumaste esos dos números. Aquí se piden grupos de algo, y eso es multiplicar. ¿Cuántos grupos hay y de qué tamaño es cada uno?

op-divided-instead-of-multiplied.label: Divided when the problem multiplies
op-divided-instead-of-multiplied.watchFor: Estimate first — should the answer be bigger or smaller than you started?
op-divided-instead-of-multiplied.student: It looks like you divided. Estimate before you compute: should this answer end up bigger or smaller than what you started with?
op-divided-instead-of-multiplied.studentEs: Parece que dividiste. Estima antes de calcular: ¿la respuesta debe ser más grande o más pequeña que con lo que empezaste?

op-multiplied-instead-of-added.label: Multiplied when the problem adds
op-multiplied-instead-of-added.watchFor: Have them restate the problem as a story, then name the operation.
op-multiplied-instead-of-added.student: It looks like you multiplied. This problem puts two amounts together, so it adds. Try telling it back as a story first, then pick the operation.
op-multiplied-instead-of-added.studentEs: Parece que multiplicaste. Este problema junta dos cantidades, así que se suma. Cuéntalo como una historia primero y luego escoge la operación.

op-multiplied-instead-of-divided.label: Multiplied when the problem divides
op-multiplied-instead-of-divided.watchFor: Estimate first — should the answer be bigger or smaller than you started?
op-multiplied-instead-of-divided.student: It looks like you multiplied. Estimate before you compute: should this answer end up bigger or smaller than what you started with?
op-multiplied-instead-of-divided.studentEs: Parece que multiplicaste. Estima antes de calcular: ¿la respuesta debe ser más grande o más pequeña que con lo que empezaste?

op-reversed-division.label: Divided in the wrong order
op-reversed-division.watchFor: Ask “what is being split, and into how many?” before they write it.
op-reversed-division.student: The two numbers got swapped in the division. Ask yourself: what is being split up? That number goes first.
op-reversed-division.studentEs: Los dos números se intercambiaron en la división. Pregúntate: ¿qué se está repartiendo? Ese número va primero.

op-reversed-subtraction.label: Subtracted in the wrong order
op-reversed-subtraction.watchFor: Anchor both numbers on a number line before subtracting.
op-reversed-subtraction.student: You subtracted in the other order. Check which amount you started with — that one goes first.
op-reversed-subtraction.studentEs: Restaste en el orden contrario. Fíjate con cuál cantidad empezaste: esa va primero.

order-of-operations-left-to-right.label: Worked left to right instead of by operation order
order-of-operations-left-to-right.labelEs: Trabajó de izquierda a derecha en vez de por orden de operaciones
order-of-operations-left-to-right.watchFor: Have them circle the operation that must go first, then compute.
order-of-operations-left-to-right.student: You worked straight across from left to right. Circle the operation that has to happen first, then compute.
order-of-operations-left-to-right.studentEs: Trabajaste de izquierda a derecha sin parar. Encierra la operación que debe hacerse primero y luego calcula.

percent-scale-off-by-100.label: Percent answer off by a factor of 100
percent-scale-off-by-100.labelEs: Respuesta de porcentaje errada por un factor de 100
percent-scale-off-by-100.watchFor: Benchmark against 50% and 10% before trusting the number.
percent-scale-off-by-100.student: Your answer is off by a factor of 100. Check it against something you already know: 50% is half, and 10% is one tenth.
percent-scale-off-by-100.studentEs: Tu respuesta está errada por un factor de 100. Compárala con algo que ya sabes: 50% es la mitad y 10% es una décima parte.

percent-used-as-whole-number.label: Used the percent as a plain number
percent-used-as-whole-number.labelEs: Usó el porcentaje como número entero
percent-used-as-whole-number.watchFor: Make them say the percent as “per hundred” out loud.
percent-used-as-whole-number.student: The percent got used as a plain number. Say it out loud as “per hundred” — 15% means 15 out of every 100, not 15.
percent-used-as-whole-number.studentEs: El porcentaje se usó como número común. Dilo en voz alta como “por cien”: 15% significa 15 de cada 100, no 15.

property-order-vs-grouping.label: Confused the commutative and associative properties
property-order-vs-grouping.labelEs: Confundió la propiedad conmutativa con la asociativa
property-order-vs-grouping.watchFor: Ask what actually MOVED: the order of the numbers, or the parentheses?
property-order-vs-grouping.student: Commutative changes the ORDER the numbers are written in. Associative changes the GROUPING — which pair sits inside the parentheses. Read both sides left to right and name what moved.
property-order-vs-grouping.studentEs: La conmutativa cambia el ORDEN en que se escriben los números. La asociativa cambia la AGRUPACIÓN: qué par queda dentro del paréntesis. Lee los dos lados de izquierda a derecha y di qué se movió.

rate-not-per-one.label: Gave the total instead of the unit rate
rate-not-per-one.labelEs: Dio el total en vez de la tasa unitaria
rate-not-per-one.watchFor: Ask “per ONE what?” and make them finish the sentence.
rate-not-per-one.student: That is the total, not the amount for ONE. Finish this sentence out loud: “for one ___, there is ___.”
rate-not-per-one.studentEs: Eso es el total, no la cantidad por UNO. Termina esta oración en voz alta: “por un ___, hay ___.”

ratio-as-difference.label: Combined the two amounts instead of comparing them
ratio-as-difference.labelEs: Combinó las dos cantidades en vez de compararlas
ratio-as-difference.watchFor: Have them say the comparison out loud — “for every ___ there are ___” — before writing anything.
ratio-as-difference.student: A ratio compares two amounts; it does not add or subtract them. Say it out loud first: “for every ___ there are ___.” Then write the two numbers in that order.
ratio-as-difference.studentEs: Una razón compara dos cantidades; no las suma ni las resta. Dilo primero en voz alta: “por cada ___ hay ___.” Luego escribe los dos números en ese orden.

ratio-compared-without-common-basis.label: Compared two ratios without a common basis
ratio-compared-without-common-basis.labelEs: Comparó dos razones sin una base común
ratio-compared-without-common-basis.watchFor: Ask what ONE of each is worth before either ratio is compared.
ratio-compared-without-common-basis.student: Two ratios cannot be compared side by side until they share a basis. Turn each into an amount per ONE, or scale both until their second numbers match, and then compare.
ratio-compared-without-common-basis.studentEs: Dos razones no se pueden comparar lado a lado hasta que compartan una base. Convierte cada una en una cantidad por UNO, o escala las dos hasta que sus segundos números coincidan, y luego compara.

ratio-inverted.label: Flipped the ratio
ratio-inverted.watchFor: Have them label both quantities with units before writing the ratio.
ratio-inverted.student: The ratio is flipped. Label both quantities with their units, then write them in the same order the question names them.
ratio-inverted.studentEs: La razón está invertida. Etiqueta las dos cantidades con sus unidades y escríbelas en el mismo orden en que la pregunta las nombra.

ratio-scaled-additively.label: Scaled a ratio by adding instead of multiplying
ratio-scaled-additively.labelEs: Escaló una razón sumando en vez de multiplicando
ratio-scaled-additively.watchFor: Ask what ONE batch is worth, then how many batches — a ratio grows by copies, not by steps.
ratio-scaled-additively.student: You added the same amount to both numbers. Equivalent ratios come from multiplying both parts by the same factor, not from adding to both. Ask: how many times bigger is the new amount?
ratio-scaled-additively.studentEs: Sumaste la misma cantidad a los dos números. Las razones equivalentes se hacen multiplicando las dos partes por el mismo factor, no sumando. Pregúntate: ¿cuántas veces más grande es la nueva cantidad?

sign-dropped.label: Right magnitude, lost the negative sign
sign-dropped.labelEs: Magnitud correcta, perdió el signo negativo
sign-dropped.watchFor: Place the answer on a number line — which side of zero?
sign-dropped.student: The size of your answer is right, but the negative sign went missing. Put it on a number line — which side of zero does it belong on?
sign-dropped.studentEs: El tamaño de tu respuesta está bien, pero se perdió el signo negativo. Ponla en una recta numérica: ¿de qué lado del cero va?

stat-center-vs-spread.label: Confused a measure of center with a measure of spread
stat-center-vs-spread.labelEs: Confundió una medida de centro con una de dispersión
stat-center-vs-spread.watchFor: Ask what the question wants to know: a typical value, or how scattered the data is?
stat-center-vs-spread.student: Those two answer different questions. A measure of center says what a typical value is; a measure of spread says how far apart the values are. Read the question again and decide which one it is asking for.
stat-center-vs-spread.studentEs: Esas dos responden preguntas distintas. Una medida de centro dice cuál es un valor típico; una de dispersión dice qué tan separados están los valores. Vuelve a leer la pregunta y decide cuál te piden.

stat-frequency-vs-value.label: Reported a data value where a frequency was asked
stat-frequency-vs-value.labelEs: Dio un valor de los datos donde se pedía una frecuencia
stat-frequency-vs-value.watchFor: Ask them to point at the axis their number came from before they answer.
stat-frequency-vs-value.student: That number came from the wrong axis. The bar's height counts HOW MANY, and the label underneath says WHICH values. The question is asking how many. Read the height, not the label.
stat-frequency-vs-value.studentEs: Ese número viene del eje equivocado. La altura de la barra cuenta CUÁNTOS, y la etiqueta de abajo dice CUÁLES valores. La pregunta pide cuántos. Lee la altura, no la etiqueta.

stat-histogram-bin-misread.label: Misread the bins or the scale on a data display
stat-histogram-bin-misread.labelEs: Leyó mal los intervalos o la escala de una gráfica
stat-histogram-bin-misread.watchFor: Have them point to the interval's two endpoints and say which values belong inside it.
stat-histogram-bin-misread.student: Check the display itself before you count. Every bar belongs to one interval, and a value counts only if it falls between that interval's endpoints. Point at the endpoints and count again.
stat-histogram-bin-misread.studentEs: Revisa la gráfica antes de contar. Cada barra pertenece a un intervalo, y un valor cuenta solo si cae entre los extremos de ese intervalo. Señala los extremos y cuenta otra vez.

stat-mean-skewed-by-outlier.label: Chose the mean when an outlier distorts it
stat-mean-skewed-by-outlier.labelEs: Eligió la media cuando un valor atípico la distorsiona
stat-mean-skewed-by-outlier.watchFor: Have them cover the outlier and recompute — how far does the mean move?
stat-mean-skewed-by-outlier.student: The mean uses every value, so one unusually high or low number drags it away from what is typical. The median does not move like that. Look at the data: is there a value far from the rest?
stat-mean-skewed-by-outlier.studentEs: La media usa todos los valores, así que un número inusualmente alto o bajo la aleja de lo típico. La mediana no se mueve así. Mira los datos: ¿hay un valor muy alejado de los demás?

stat-mean-vs-median.label: Used the mean where the median was asked (or the reverse)
stat-mean-vs-median.labelEs: Usó la media donde se pedía la mediana (o al revés)
stat-mean-vs-median.watchFor: Ask them to say which word the question used, then what that word tells you to DO with the numbers.
stat-mean-vs-median.student: Those are two different measures. The mean adds every value and divides; the median puts the values in order and takes the middle one. Read the question again and name which one it asked for.
stat-mean-vs-median.studentEs: Esas son dos medidas distintas. La media suma todos los valores y divide; la mediana ordena los valores y toma el del medio. Vuelve a leer la pregunta y di cuál te pidió.

stat-question-no-variability.label: Chose a question with only one fixed answer
stat-question-no-variability.labelEs: Escogió una pregunta con una sola respuesta fija
stat-question-no-variability.watchFor: Ask: would two different people give two different answers?
stat-question-no-variability.student: A statistical question expects answers that VARY. That one has a single fixed answer, so there is no data to collect. Ask what would change from one person to the next.
stat-question-no-variability.studentEs: Una pregunta estadística espera respuestas que VARÍEN. Esa tiene una sola respuesta fija, así que no hay datos que recoger. Pregúntate qué cambiaría de una persona a otra.

stat-range-for-iqr.label: Used the full range instead of the IQR
stat-range-for-iqr.labelEs: Usó el rango completo en vez del rango intercuartílico
stat-range-for-iqr.watchFor: Have them mark Q1 and Q3 on the plot and cover everything outside them.
stat-range-for-iqr.student: That is the whole spread, from the smallest value to the largest. The IQR only measures the middle half: it is Q3 − Q1, and it ignores the extremes entirely. Find those two quartiles and subtract.
stat-range-for-iqr.studentEs: Esa es la dispersión completa, del valor más pequeño al más grande. El rango intercuartílico solo mide la mitad central: es Q3 − Q1 e ignora por completo los extremos. Halla esos dos cuartiles y resta.

stat-summed-instead-of-averaged.label: Added the data set instead of averaging it
stat-summed-instead-of-averaged.labelEs: Sumó el conjunto de datos en vez de promediarlo
stat-summed-instead-of-averaged.watchFor: Ask whether the answer could be a realistic single value in that set.
stat-summed-instead-of-averaged.student: That is the total of the data, not its average. Could your answer be one realistic value from that list? An average has to land inside the data.
stat-summed-instead-of-averaged.studentEs: Eso es el total de los datos, no su promedio. ¿Tu respuesta podría ser un valor real de esa lista? Un promedio tiene que caer dentro de los datos.
